summary: Where a number comes from, such as a system, a register, a ledger or a survey.
example: Sales Ledger, where member season earnings are read from.
definition: A place a number comes from: a register, a system, a survey, a record or a set of documents. KPIs, key results, gaps and success criteria name the data source they take numbers from. It says what type of source it is, who runs it, and how records get into it, which decides how soon a number can be known. It is not a KPI (the measure itself), not a report made from sources, and not the team that keeps it.

/metadata/name.guide: The name people use for this source.

poor.why: That is the type of source. Name the spreadsheet itself, such as the Collection Log.

poor.text: Share of deliveries checked at intake
poor.why: That is a measure, so it is a KPI. Name where its numbers come from.

/spec/category.guide: What type of source this is: a database, a spreadsheet, a paper record, a form or survey, a system used to run the work, an API or feed, or a set of documents.

poor.why: Chosen for the Depot Maintenance Log, a logbook kept at each depot. It is a paper record until somebody types it in.

/spec/provenance.guide: Internal if your organisation runs this source, external if someone outside it does.

poor.why: The finance team is part of your organisation, so the Sales Ledger is internal. External means someone outside your organisation runs it.

/spec/team.guide: The team in your organisation that keeps this source. Choose a team, not a person or role.

poor.why: A role, not a team. Choose the team that keeps the source.

/spec/access.guide: How someone gets to read it, and what they need first: who to ask, what account, whether it is a copy or the source itself.
good: Shared spreadsheet, one tab per depot, filled in by the depot supervisor.
Read access on request from the finance team.

poor.why: Names a person. Say which role or team to ask, and how access is given.
Says that access exists, not how anyone gets it.

/spec/refresh.guide: How often the contents change: daily, weekly, monthly, termly, quarterly, annual, or irregular when there is no set rhythm. A number from this source cannot change more often than this.

poor.why: Chosen for the Member Survey, which runs once a season on a known rhythm. Irregular is for a source that changes with no rhythm at all.

/spec/capture.guide: How records get into the source: typed in by hand, scanned from paper, filled in online, fed from another system, or not decided yet. This decides how soon a number from it can be known.

poor.why: Chosen for the Quality Check Tool. Its forms start on paper and are typed into a spreadsheet later, so they are typed in by hand.

/spec/classification.guide: How sensitive the contents are: public, internal, confidential or restricted. Leave it empty if you are not sure.

poor.text: Internal use only, but some fields are sensitive
poor.why: Pick one level: the highest that applies to anything in the source.

/spec/qualityIssues.guide: What is known to be wrong with the source: what is missing, late, rounded or skewed, and since when.
good: Collection times are entered by hand and are sometimes rounded to the hour.
Answered by roughly half the membership, weighted towards larger holdings.
Entries stop when a depot is short staffed, which is when they matter most.

poor.why: Too vague. Say what is wrong and since when.
Leave it empty if no problems are known yet.

/spec/keptBy.guide: The outside body that keeps this source, such as an agency or a partner. Leave it empty if your own team keeps it.

poor.text: The team field set to an outside body
poor.why: Team must be one of your own teams. Name the outside body as the keeper instead.

KPI:/spec/sources.ask: Which KPIs take their numbers from this source?
KPI:/spec/sources.ifNone: None yet is fine. Gaps, key results and success criteria can also use a source, and a KPI names this source when it uses it.
